hints: A run like 1, 2, 3, 4 has exactly one value where it begins. How can you tell that a value is the start of a run?
Put all values in a hash set. A value x starts a run only when x − 1 is missing; from each start, count upward while x + 1, x + 2, … are present.

1. Insert every value into a set.
  2. For each value x in the set: skip it if x − 1 is in the set.
  3. Otherwise walk y = x upward while y + 1 is in the set, counting.
  4. Keep the largest count.
  5. Print it.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: From every value, keep searching the array for the next value up; each search is a linear scan.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Sort, then scan counting consecutive steps of +1 and skipping duplicates.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Hash set; only start counting at values whose predecessor is missing, so each value is walked over once.

explain: For 100 4 200 1 3 2, the set holds all six values. 1 has no 0 before it, so we walk 1→2→3→4 and get length 4. 2, 3 and 4 are skipped because their predecessors exist, which is why the total work stays linear. 100 and 200 each start a run of length 1. Use long or care with x − 1 at the edge of the int range; values here are only up to 109, so int is safe.
recognize: "Longest consecutive values, unsorted, aim for O(N)" → hash set plus counting only from run starts.
python:
import sys
data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = data[0]
s = set(data[1:1 + n])
best = 0
for x in s:
    if x - 1 in s:  # not the start of a run
        continue
    length = 1
    while x + length in s:
        length += 1
    best = max(best, length)
print(best)
